thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 - Elevated backend errors and timeouts impacting quasar-8b family (hosted API). Auto-alert triggered by 5xx spike and token-timeout rate. Paging on-call.
alyssa: I'm oncall, pulling dashboards now. which endpoints?
samir: main spike on /v1/generate and streaming sessions. 5xx increased from ~0.2% to 6% over last 3m, p99 latencies up ~6x. KCQ shows KV cache misses for quasar-8b.
leo: seeing higher queuing on GPU pools backing quasar-8b. Some requests getting routed to fallback slower nodes -> elevated tail.
alyssa: do we have a quick mitigation? per-model throttling?
leo: recommend immediate TPM cap for quasar-8b to prevent head-of-line congestion. Propose: reduce global TPM for quasar-8b from 800 -> 200 (25%). Also disable streaming for that family as a quick throttle (streaming multiplies open connections).
samir: +1 on TPM cap. Also add per-customer soft-quotas for high-burst tenants. We can push a routing rule to send low-priority requests to quasar-8b-quant fallback.
alyssa: ok execute. runbook step: use redwoodctl to set emergency tpm. I'll coordinate.
alyssa: ```
# emergency TPM cap
redwoodctl quota set --model-family quasar-8b --tpm 200 --scope global --reason "emergency incident 2851234567"
# disable streaming for family
redwoodctl feature-toggle set --model-family quasar-8b --feature streaming --state off
```
ops-bot: Applying quota change: set quasar-8b global TPM=200 by alyssa (req 2851234567).
ops-bot: Streaming toggle applied: quasar-8b streaming=off.
nina: quick sanity check on customer impact: one high-volume customer (AcmeAI) on Dedicated path saw increased error rate earlier, but they're on dedicated pool unaffected. Hosted customers are the main ones impacted. I've posted to #support to flag increased 5xx for hosted customers.
jordan: added a short note to incident doc: reduced quasar-8b TPM to 200 and streaming disabled. monitoring links: https://console.redwood/ops/incidents/2851234567 and dashboards -> token-error-rate, pool-queue-depth.
alyssa: good. eng-sre-oncall, can you take over the mitigation monitoring and follow roll-forward plan? I'll keep this channel for customer comms.
eng-sre-oncall: taking. will watch 1m/5m error rates and p99; plan to incrementally restore if queues drop below threshold (queue_depth < 12) for 10m continuous. Also starting a canary routing: route 10% of low-priority requests back to quasar-8b if healthy.
samir: created temporary traffic-shaper rule (priority-based): low-priority -> quasar-8b-quant fallback, medium/high -> respect new TPM cap. snippet: ```
trafficctl add-rule --name quasar-burst-control --match "model_family=quasar-8b" --action "rate_limit=200,tier=per_family,priority_policy=prefer_fallback"
```
ops-bot: traffic rule quasar-burst-control applied.
alyssa: monitoring update after 3m: overall error rate fell from 6% -> 1.4%, p99 latency dropped ~40%. Good. Any observed functional regressions from disabling streaming?
leo: one internal test shows stream->non-stream fallback increases response-size CPU use but ok for now. Need to watch memory in frontends.
nina: support already contacted 3 customers with elevated latencies and told them we're throttling specific model family to stabilize. No escalations yet.
jordan: logging note: recorded mitigation actions and who executed them (alyssa). Will attach CLI logs to the incident doc.
eng-sre-oncall: continuing monitoring. If we see sustained stability for 15m, we'll attempt staged rollback: raise TPM to 400, re-enable streaming for canary subset. Rollout plan: +50% TPM every 10m if error rate <0.5% and queue_depth<10.
alyssa: handoff: i'm signing off active mitigation coordination in 10m. @eng-sre-oncall own the incident for now. I'll be reachable for customer comms.
samir: follow-up items: investigate root cause - KV cache invalidation pattern for quasar-8b, and a recent kernel update that might have changed batching behavior. Create follow-up ticket.
alyssa: thanks team. keep updates short here. :thumbsup:
